identity.name: Armenian Soviet Socialist Republic
native_names: Հայկական Սովետական Սոցիալիստական Հանրապետություն (Haykakan Sovetakan Sotsialistakan Hanrapetutyun)

land.text: Cliopatria's Armenia of 1919, the First Republic of Armenia (40,911 km2)

predecessors.note: Soviet Armenia was established on 29 November 1920 "with the Sovietisation of the short-lived First Republic of Armenia".

successors.note: Declared state sovereignty and renamed Hayastani Hanrapetutyun on 23 August 1990; independence referendum 21 September 1991; recognised 26 December 1991.

capitals.name: Yerevan
capitals.note: "The capital of the republic was Yerevan."

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 29,336 km2 (the Natural Earth country; the page gives no area): Soviet Armenia in the borders it held after the Treaty of Kars (13 October 1921) to 1991. Cliopatria's Armenia of 1919 is 40,911 km2 and ends in 1919; the Soviet years lie inside its Union of Soviet Socialist Republics shapes. The Armenian page is silent on Zangezur (Syunik), so the modern republic's southern province is drawn from the start; the Kars region, Ardahan and the Surmalu district, which "Turkey obtained", are not drawn. [Reviewer eu-17-x: this keyframe now ends in 1921; from 12 March 1922 to 5 December 1936 the land is the Transcaucasian SFSR's (ledger loss and gain, and that dossier's keyframe); the same shape resumes in the 1937 keyframe.]

ledger.note: 1920, 29 November: "Soviet Armenia was established on 29 November 1920, with the Sovietisation of the short-lived First Republic of Armenia"; on 2 December Yerevan signed a pact with Moscow "securing Armenian statehood as a Soviet republic".

region.text: Armenia within Natural Earth borders, including Syunik (Zangezur)

ledger.note: 1922, March: the Armenian SSR enters the Transcaucasian federation ("From March 1922 to December 1936, Soviet Armenia formed part of the" TSFSR; the infobox gives 30 December 1922).

region.text: Armenia within Natural Earth borders, including Syunik (Zangezur)

ledger.note: 1936, 5 December: "When the TSFSR was dissolved in 1936, Armenia became a constituent republic of the Soviet Union" (infobox "Re-established: 5 December 1936"); the name becomes Armenian Soviet Socialist Republic.

1990, 23 August: "Local authorities declared state sovereignty on 23 August 1990"; the formal name is declared Hayastani Hanrapetutyun (the infobox: "Independence declared, Renamed Republic of Armenia: 23 August 1990").

region.text: Armenia within Natural Earth borders, including Syunik (Zangezur)

ledger.note: 1991, 21 September: "An independence referendum held on 21 September 1991 was supported by more than 99% of voters"; independence was recognised 26 December 1991 (the infobox dates the declaration to 23 August 1990).

certainty.note: Alexandropol talks with Turkey (December 1920) and the Treaty of Kars (13 October 1921) fixed the western border; the Zangezur and Karabakh lines are not on the pages opened.
Kars border with Turkey; the Azerbaijan border is the Soviet-era internal line, drawn as the modern one.

sources.title: Armenian Soviet Socialist Republic
sources.note: 29 November 1920; 2 December pact; Kars and Surmalu ceded to Turkey; TSFSR March 1922 (text) or 30 December 1922 (infobox); 5 December 1936; sovereignty 23 August 1990; referendum 21 September 1991; capital Yerevan; no area; silent on Zangezur.

sources.title: Treaty of Kars
sources.note: 13 October 1921: Turkey obtained the Kars oblast (Kars, Ardahan, Oltu), the Surmalu uezd with Mount Ararat and Igdir; the page does not name the ceding party.

sources.title: Transcaucasian Socialist Federative Soviet Republic
sources.note: Established 12 March 1922; dissolved 5 December 1936; area 186,043 km2.

notes: No Cliopatria row after 1919 (Cliopatria's Armenia is 1918-1919; its Republic of Armenia is 1992 on); the Soviet years lie inside Union of Soviet Socialist Republics shapes. The republic is an internal unit of the Soviet Union. The western border is drawn at the Natural Earth line, which is the Treaty of Kars border; the Kars oblast, Ardahan, Surmalu (Igdir, with Mount Ararat) and Ani went to Turkey, but no page opened says the Armenian SSR held them, so no loss is entered (the Armenian SSR page calls them "the Armenian regions" and the Kars page does not name the ceding party). The Turkish side is for a Turkey dossier. Dates disagree: joining the TSFSR is March 1922 in the text and 30 December 1922 in the infobox; independence is "declared" on 23 August 1990 (infobox) and confirmed by the referendum of 21 September 1991, which is used as the end. Not on any page opened: Zangezur, the Nagorno-Karabakh transfer, Lori and Karabakh border lines, area. Counterparts: armenia and republic-of-armenia exist (Cliopatria).
